scope: Persisted superadmin global-list and cross-tenant direct-read access plus Tenant B Brand/Team/User lifecycle in API and Cloud.

environment.database: Separate disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 databases for API and Cloud on localhost.
environment.tenants: Synthetic Tenant A and Tenant B only.
environment.network: Only local HTTP services and the isolated PostgreSQL cluster; no customer/provider endpoint.

assertions_per_backend: Registered a synthetic account and observed the default role=user before isolating and promoting the fixture to superadmin in the test database.
Superadmin global list routes returned Company, Brand, Team and User collections; both Companies and both tenant Brands were identified, along with Tenant B Team and User records.
Superadmin read Tenant B Brand, Team and User by direct ID.
Created and deleted a Brand and Team under Tenant B.
Created a Tenant B User as role=user, received admin from a superadmin update request, read the user detail without password/hash/token/secret fields, and deleted it.
Deleted the temporary superadmin fixture and verified zero UAT-076 users, Brands and Teams remained in PostgreSQL.
limitations: This validates selected superadmin operations across two tenants and three resource families; it does not close the full 39-model × role × surface × operation matrix.

Brand/Team update was verified separately for Tenant A in UAT-075; this UAT-076 cross-tenant journey covers global lists, Tenant B direct reads, create and delete. User role assignment was verified from the update response; a separate database assertion of the final role was not included in this case.
